column2: In 1914, one Christmas song made a hundred thousand enemies stop shooting.
It's Christmas Eve on the Western Front. Five months of mud, rats and shelling. The enemy trench is close enough to shout across.
Then the Germans put candles along their trench. Little Christmas trees. And they start singing.
The British sing back. Someone shouts, Merry Christmas! And one man climbs out. Unarmed.
You see, in a trench, everyone copies the man next to them. When a few men went first, the next trench copied them. Then the next. For miles.
They swapped cigarettes, food and buttons. They buried their dead together. Some even kicked a ball around. In one account, the ball was a tin of beef.
The generals were furious. The next Christmas, they ordered the artillery to fire, just so it couldn't happen again.
Because peace spreads the same way war does. Somebody goes first.
